draft.text: You came in because you have been having trouble breathing more than usual and pain when swallowing.
This has been getting worse over the weekend and is making it hard to do daily activities.
During the exam, we heard crackles in your lungs, which might mean there is fluid there.
We did not find any swollen lymph nodes in your neck.
Your symptoms may be related to radiation-induced lung injury and esophagitis.
These are conditions that can happen after cancer treatments and can cause trouble breathing and pain when swallowing.
We will think about ordering tests like an endoscopy or a barium swallow to look at your esophagus and check for any problems.
You will keep using lidocaine for pain relief and we will watch how your symptoms change.

unverified_summary.text: You came in because you have been having trouble breathing more than before, and you have pain when you swallow.
We did not do any tests or check your body measurements during this visit.
Your symptoms may be related to changes in your lungs from treatment and possible irritation in your esophagus.
We will talk about possible tests to look at your esophagus and lungs.
You will keep using medicine for pain, and we will watch your symptoms closely.
We may also think about changing your treatment plan.
